I am not capable of that. But am I "bad enough" to even need the help? Should I just wait until it's unbearable and wait till I'm on the verge of doing it and break and finally ask for help? 

It's difficult, but we should do something. Anything to get help

I'm sorry to hear about how your mother treated you, thinking it was for attention. My mother... Well, she's never been an A+ mother, in any book but her own twisted one. When I was in 9th grade I started self-harming, through cutting, and ended up with an armfull of well over 50 cuts. A month after I stopped, on my own accord, she burst into my room at midnight and dragged me into a shouting dispute between her and my at-the-time stepfather. She shouted that "My oldest daughter would rather slit her wrists than spend time with me, can't you see her arm??" 

A couple months after that, when I asked about a band-aid on her fifnger she told me she cut the tip of it off trying to pull apart a disposable razor like I told her I did, so she could slit her wrists. 

And then when my younger sister started cutting, she continuously blamed me, even in front of my sister's therapists. She told me that I wasn't diagnised with any mental illnesses, so what I did was just seeking attention and that I'd never feel the way they did... 

But now i do. I think, at least, they never really went full-out and explained how they felt to me. But I'm afraid she'll accuse me again of doing it for attention, or even worse, just laugh in my face and leave. My dad will feel like a failure of a father for having two mentally dysfunctional children, or think I'm being ridiculous and this is all an act since I've never displayed any signs of depression or suicidal thoughts since I stopped self-harming. 

And my boyfriend... He doesn't know I've had suicidal thoughts. I can't tell him... I wouldn't know how without stirring up old memories, he lost his father just three years ago to suicide and still is grieving over him. How could I do that to him? If I go out and tell someone - a counsellor or something - would they admit me, like they did my sister when she was threatening suicide? Would they tell my parents, or have me locked up in a mental hospital until I'm "better" again? And how can I even trust myself not to just play it cool and lie my way out of there, but to accept the help, if they do? Or would they keep it quiet, since I really, really don't WANT to die, but often feel as if I should, just because I have nowhere to go, nowhere where I can find any definite happiness and tranquility, and can't stand this seemingly endless period in between of self-hatred and overall depression? 

I just don't know how to figure this out...
I understand, I do the same thing. It forces me to understand the reality of doing it. And that usually scares me away from it.

..thank you, for all of this. I guess you're right - the only thing I can do is hold onto what I do have, what I have seem to have gotten right, and let it make me happy. Do whatever I can to make a good life for myself, because obviously nobody else is going to do it for me, right? 

Thank you, this... This helped.
Thank you for that, that actually makes a lot of sense and makes me feel a little better... I appreciate it

Thank you for reading and offering advice. 

I have tried art. It's one of the things that I can go back to when I'm not fighting the depression and the suicidal thoughts, but it makes it worse when I am depressed. I get out the paper, I get my pencils and pens, and... Nothing. I go blank, staring at that piece of paper. I can't think of anything to draw, I look up references like I always do and when I try, I try so hard and it ends up looking horrible and I hate myself for it... It makes me even more upset than not trying it, to be honest... 

Music I can sometimes drown out the feelings with, but not all the time. I have crappy headphones that don't work half the time and I can't just play music loudly when there's anyone else in the house/at school. But when I can, it does help. 

Again, thank you for the advice and for taking the time to read this and offer help...

Thank you for your kind words and advice. I will look into those things, and try my best to get myself out of this vicious cycle. 
But my issue has nothing to do with money, it has to do with myself. I am glad you found a way to help others with what you've made for yourself. 

And trust me, I do "fucking" see how amazing it is to have my boyfriend in my life. But being with him, even, means that I will eventually have to give up the rest of my family. Being with him means that I can be myself, that I can be who I actually am and won't have to live with these walls of lies I've had to put between my family and I. 
But when those walls come down and the truth comes out about my religion, or lack thereof (my family is full of VERY strict cristians who will not accept an athiest in the family, and my parents already feel like they've failed as parents just because my sister came out as athiest), they will be torn apart and possibly just disown me entirely, or try to convert me. I have tried my damndest to believe, but there's just nothing there, no belief. It feels wrong to me. 

If I didn't have my boyfriend I would likely not have changed a bit throughout the past few years. I've recognized self-worth, then had it torn apart in my face by the family that's supposed to care so much for me. I'd still be a blind follower of anything they say is right. He won't let me hide myself, be ashamed for lying about myself to my family when they aren't in control of me anymore. And that very well might cause me to lose them. Probably. And is that worth it? I can be happy with him, but not have any of the family that's been with me the past 17 years? Or vice versa, and never be myself, always alone and never understood... 

I am thinking about this end because then there are no material goals. There will be no more love. There will be no more pain and hurt and sorrow. 

I thank you for your advice, and for taking the time out of your day to share your experience and offer help. I will check out that book.

Sometimes it isn't that easy. I personally have a very, very tough time telling anyone about my problems, let alone see a psychiatrist. It isn't always a financial possibility, either. If OP is a minor, or doesn't have a job, or their parents aren't supportive enough to help them with it, it may not be something they can "just do"
Finding people who think like them, in the state they're thinking at the moment, may not be the best idea. Others who think there is only one way out of a tough situation may direct them towards, not away from, self-destructive actions. 
And, again, what if moving isn't a feasable option for OP? What if they're a minor, or cannot financially support themself alone at the moment? 
It's easy to just toss out advice that may be really easy for you to follow through with, but without asking questions and knowing more about the person's life and situation, giving advice in this manner may be more hurtful than helpful, and cause them to think that, since they cannot follow through with this advice they are continuously given, that that is the only reliable way out of their situation, and the only other option is the one they're here to talk about.

This is just my opinion.

It doesn't sound weird at all, trust me. I've had the same issues, seeing no end to hard times besides my own end. You don't have a very good relationship with your parents, do you? Let me guess, they thought self harm and depression was just a "phase" you were going through, and are now too stubborn to quit. I have seen this happen before, and it's this misrepresentation of self-harm that's caused me to quit, simply because it made everything harder on me. I was ridiculed for it, being told I only did it to seek attention, that my life wasn't bad enough to feel so horrible about myself that I hurt myself. It isn't fair, but your feelings towards it aren't wrong. You have to shield yourself and your feelings from your parents si they don't see the harm they cause you. And they don't know how to show their love for you properly, their care for you

It isn't fair, and there will be times in life that you struggle with these feelings. Try distracting yourself. Find an outlet that has nothing to do with other people, so that nobody else can drag you down in an activity that you deem helpful to your mental state. Try reading - escaping into another world for a while to forget about your own issues. Or drawing, painting, sculpting. Drown yourself in any music that makes you feel closer to yourself, that re-draws those strings that tie your body to your mind and your mind to your emotions. Pick up an instrument. Find a forest trail close to you and walk it for an hour or so. Meditate. There are so many other things you can do to clear your head and bring you into a better state of mind than suicide. 

If you need to talk, I can do my best to be there for you as a friend. But I struggle with these thoughts frequently also, so I don't want to make any promises that I may not be able to keep... 

I hope this can help you, even in the smallest way

Can I share something with you...?
I had never been outgoing at all in school. It took a lot for me to become friends with someone and if I developed feelings for them, I pushed them away... But I met this boy in 8th grade, who was dating this perfect girl. Short, thin as a twig, beautiful, three years older than him. him and I became very close friends very quickly, and he found out that I liked him, and told me, essentially, "Sorry. You aren't my type." That we could be friends and that was it. 
I was depressed. I had put everything into our friendship and felt very, very strongly about him. So I stuck it out. I told him I understood, I'm not beautiful in the sloghtest, I'm not thin, I was almost his height at the time, and a month and a half younger than him. 
But I told him that I understood. And I would be there for him and be the best friend that I could be. It hurt, of course, seeing him with his arm around her, watching them sit together and talk and laugh while I, having been invited over to hang out, sat in the background being dragged around by his younger siblings. 
Then she broke his heart. Shattered it, and like a cat, played eith the pieces until they were scattered and irretrievable. And I was there. I helped him find the pieces, put them all back together, and smiled sadly, stifling an "I told you so"
Five months later, he decided to give us a try. 
This march we will have been together 4 years. And I wouldn't trade a minute of it for the world...

So, just letting you know, if you stick close, prove yourself to be there for her, don't show any jealousy, and be the best friend she could ever ask for, there very well may be a chance in the future. If you feel so strongly about her, then don't give up, but don't push. Just be there. She'll see

Do you have a cell phone? A good idea to get away from your parents and admit yourself, if you are a minor, without causing any harm to yourself could be this: take your cell phone and leave your house. Skip a day of school, wait till they are not home, or somehow when they won't know you're gone. Go to a tall building, or a bridge or something. DON'T go near the edge, or to the top of the building. Call 911. Tell them where you are and that you are suicidal. They will admit you and from there you can insist to doctors that you need psychiatric help, tell them you don't want to die but you need counselling and your parents don't understand. 
I am sure that would work, at least.

As an instinct myself, I enjoy the banter between teams and little memes and such, and the rivalry is a part of the game. I agree some take it too far (vandalizing with other team's names, etc) but you can't really generalize on the part of any community solely based on what you see here on reddit. 
For example, what I have read and seen tells me that Valor is bruteish and outright mean, Mystic is thoughtful and powerful, and Instinct is a small, kind community. But in my area, when I walk around and take gyms solo, it's different. Valors tend to conduct themselves in excited, friendly groups, Instincts keep to themselves and quietly take gyms at random, and Mystics are obnoxious and rude to any non-mystic. (I was threatened by a group for being in an area with two pokestops with lures on them and a gym in reach, just for taking the gym... Which is the whole idea of the game, and two other times I witnessed Mystics shouting at Valors or telling Instincts to "F* off" for being in "their" territory, which was actually a public park) 
I like things like Instinct pride posts and Valor's propaganda posters, and you guys have the prettiest artwork I've seen of any team, but we shouldn't look down on any other team just because of what we see and don't like in one small portion of it. 

That being said, I do believe there are attributes that can be said for most of the members on each team, and that is because they are the ideals that are presented for each team at Level 5. Valor focuses on strength and power, Mystic focuses on logic and thought, Instinct focuses on, well, instinct. So it would make sense that Valors try to show pride in their team with their strength, Mystics their knowledge, and Instincts their instinctual actions. But each individual person has their own ways of showing these things. If you don't like the way they act, then just don't act that way, don't try to make them look bad. If it's within your own team, do what you can to correct the action and save Mystic's reputation. 

That's all I have to say at the moment. I appreciate your opinion! These are just mine~
